messages:
Jing: Heads-up — planning a small canary tomorrow to surface the effective auth identity in the Console request view. Idea is to show which principal actually billed the request (org API key / project SA / proxy). Will only be on 10% of traffic and behind a flag. Thoughts?

Ravi: +1. This would help a lot for quota disputes. Quick Q: are we computing effective identity at the gateway or in the auth proxy?

Jing: We'll compute it in auth-proxy (where we do exchange) so it matches billing attribution. We already annotate requests with an X-Effective-Principal header; Console will display that. Example header: `X-Effective-Principal: sa:proj-42:deploy-bot`

Alex: Nice. UX note — show both the original key and the effective principal (small muted text) so support can see the chain. Otherwise people assume the key on the request was the billable one.

Sam: Telemetry question: how will this get into our metering pipeline? We need to ensure the billing key and effective principal are both emitted to prometheus/ingest. Otherwise dashboards will mismatch.

Jing: Plan is to emit both as tags on the request metric in the gateway: `billing_key` and `effective_principal`. We'll also emit a boolean `effective_differs` when they diverge.

Ravi: That boolean will be super useful. Can we add a sanity-check alert when >1% of traffic has `effective_differs=true` for a tenant? Might indicate token-exchange bugs or impersonation.

Alex: For the Console rollout, make the new column filterable and add a tooltip explaining why they might differ (exchange, fallback, impersonation). Also add a small link to the playbook: /docs/console/auth-visibility

Sam: Also: quota enforcement. If effective principal maps to a project that has exhausted quota, we must show the real reason in the UI and not just "quota exceeded" generically. Otherwise customers open support tickets.

Jing: Agreed. We'll surface the quota owner and the specific limit that blocked the request. That will require a join between quota-mgr events and the request trace — doable in the canary region only.

Ravi: Rollout plan sanity check: 10% traffic, opt-out per-org flag, and a monitoring dashboard to compare billing attribution before/after. Who owns the dashboard?

Alex: Ping me — I can wire up a dashboard with two panels: attribution delta by org, and top principals where they differ.

Sam: One more: privacy. Displaying raw SA ids in Console could leak internal names. Suggest we hash-long-id and show friendly alias + truncated id. e.g., `sa:my-service (sa-xxxx...)`

Jing: Good call. We'll show `display_name (short-id)` and keep full id in support logs only.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: auth-proxy/service v1.12.3 -> canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC. Flag `console.auth_effective_principal` default=false.

Jing: Thanks — I'll follow up with the Console PR and the canary playbook. Will post the playbook link once ready. :rocket:

Ravi: Thanks — let's also add the alert rule for `effective_differs > 1%` in the canary cluster so we catch anything weird early.

Alex: I'll start the dashboard draft and share a link in this thread before the deploy.

Sam: 👍 keep the opt-out per-org and ensure support role can opt-out on request.

Jing: Will do. End-to-end checklist: header emitted, metrics tags + `effective_differs`, console UI column + tooltip + truncation, quota-owner surface, dashboard + alert, canary flag.

Alex: Sounds good.

Jing: Cool — moving to canary. Feel free to DM if you want to review the PR.
